o1.biggest_strength: It puts the in-app checkout bug first with correct money (558 orders, about ₹34 lakh margin at ₹6,090 each), calls it a ceiling, and shows its sample-size working.
o1.biggest_mistake: It runs every test on all devices with orders as the only main metric, so the mobile-only size picker and hero changes get diluted by desktop traffic, and it never uses add-to-cart as a faster primary read.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Target the mobile-only changes at mobile traffic, use add-to-cart as the primary metric for top-of-page tests, and break down the funnel by segment to show where each leak sits.

o2.biggest_strength: A correct stage-by-stage funnel table by segment shows in-app add-to-cart is normal and the leak is cart to checkout. Matching the roughly 4,130 in-app errors to the 4,800 lost carts nails the bug, sized at ₹34 lakh margin.
o2.biggest_mistake: The review block appears both in the ship list (rating under the name) and in Test 5, which blurs what that test is measuring.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Separate the reviews-up change cleanly from the hero test, and give each test's minimum detectable effect in rupees of gross margin, not just percent.

reason: Both find the checkout bug and price it right, but the second shows me exactly where each segment leaks. It also targets mobile tests at mobile, and uses add-to-cart where a page change should be read fast. It is the plan a real testing lead would hand me.
